claims.text: The datasource must be enabled for search.
claims.excerpt: For the indexed document to show up in Glean UI, the datasource must be enabled for search.

claims.text: Indexing tokens require an expiry date.
claims.excerpt: An expiration date is required.

claims.text: Prefer read-only keys.
claims.excerpt: read-only keys are preferred if supported for Content+Permission+Activity data

claims.text: Self-hosted networking must allow pushes to Glean indexing endpoints.
claims.excerpt: Your environment must allow pushes to Glean's indexing endpoints.

claims.text: First-run: one public, then one permissioned document, then scale.
claims.excerpt: Index a single public sample document and confirm it appears in search. Then index one permissioned document and confirm only authorized users can see it. Once both behave correctly, scale up.

claims.text: Choose the permissions model at setup.
claims.excerpt: Permissions model - whether documents are permission-aware (per-user ACLs pushed with each document) or visible to everyone in the org.

claims.text: urlRegex must be neither too broad nor too narrow.
claims.excerpt: Avoid regexes that are too broad, and will capture URLs from other datasources, or regexes that are too narrow

claims.text: isUserReferencedByEmail decides email vs ID references.
claims.excerpt: This should be set to true if you want to refer to user identities using emails directly.

claims.text: Datasource category affects ranking.
claims.excerpt: Choosing the appropriate type enables enhanced ranking.

claims.text: Beta users still need document permissions.
claims.excerpt: For a document to be visible to beta users, they must also have appropriate permissions to view it.

claims.text: Test datasources have ranking signals off.
claims.excerpt: All ranking signals are turned off from a test datasource.

claims.text: Indexing API accepts only Glean-issued tokens.
claims.excerpt: The Indexing API only supports Glean-issued tokens - OAuth authentication is not available.

claims.text: Minimum token rotation period is 1440 minutes.
claims.excerpt: Minimum rotation period: 1440 minutes (24 hours)

claims.text: Automate token rotation.
claims.excerpt: Automated indexing token rotation

claims.text: Only Super Admins can grant global indexing scope.
claims.excerpt: Setup Admins, Admins, and Super Admins can create Indexing API tokens (only Super Admins can grant global scope).

claims.text: IP restrictions limit tokens to known infrastructure.
claims.excerpt: Restrict API access to known infrastructure

claims.text: Indexing tokens support IP range restrictions.
claims.excerpt: IP range restrictions for requests

claims.text: The token value is shown once.
claims.excerpt: The token is only displayed once after creation.

claims.text: Use separate tokens per environment.
claims.excerpt: Create separate tokens for different environments (dev/staging/prod)

claims.text: Ask for a sandbox.
claims.excerpt: Is there a Dev/Test/Sandbox environment against which connector development can be tested/validated?

claims.text: Ask whether the API URL is static.
claims.excerpt: Will the API URL stay static?

claims.text: Choose hosting before building.
claims.excerpt: Choose where it runs before you build, because it determines how secrets, scheduling, and networking are handled.

claims.text: Counts prove nothing about permissions.
claims.excerpt: Counting indexed documents proves nothing about permissions.

claims.text: Self-host when residency, isolation, or policy requires it.
claims.excerpt: Choose this when data-residency, network isolation, or internal security policies require the connector to run inside your infrastructure.
